sentences.text: Module one begins, and Valeria is now building Nexo herself.
Contoso asks for three new jobs.
Record invoices in an old desktop program that has no A P I.
Check live inventory in a system with an OpenAPI file.
And share those tools with other A I clients in the company.
Three systems, three very different doors.
Today you learn to pick the right bridge for each one, the base of every solution.
An agent that only chats is like an employee with no phone and no computer.
Integration bridges give it hands to read, create and update data.
Copilot Studio offers six: Power Platform connectors, already built for well known services.
Custom connectors.
The REST A P I tool.
M C P servers.
Agent flows, built inside Copilot Studio.
And computer use.
All of them show up in one place: Tools.
One question sorts almost every case: does the system expose an A P I?
If a connector already exists, use it.
If you have an OpenAPI file, use the REST A P I tool or a custom connector.
If the system speaks the M C P protocol, connect it as an M C P server.
And if it only has a screen, with no A P I at all, the answer is computer use.
When several bridges could work, go down this order.
A prebuilt connector first: no development, though large results slow the answer.
No connector, and several agents need the same A P I?
Build a custom connector you can reuse.
A one off A P I in a test?
The REST A P I tool, which is in preview and works only inside Copilot Studio.
Steps that must run in order, with human approval: an agent flow.
A central tool server for many agents: M C P.
Your turn.
Contoso's inventory system has an OpenAPI file, but no ready connector.
Three different agents need it, and a Power Automate flow needs it too.
Which bridge do they build?
A REST A P I tool inside each agent?
A custom connector they all share?
Or a Send H T T P request node per topic?
Decide before I answer.
A custom connector.
Many agents share it, and it also works in Power Automate.
The REST A P I tool lives only inside Copilot Studio.
Every bridge has a price.
Agent flows depend on A P I rate limits, need explicit error paths, limit the size of the response sent back, and use Copilot Credits.
M C P needs generative orchestration, topics cannot call it, and the tool descriptions are set on the server.
The Send H T T P request node is quick for one call, but you cannot share it.
And Bot Framework skills reuse pro code, but need C sharp, Azure costs, and sit outside Power Platform A L M.
Two bridges deserve a closer look.
M C P is an open protocol, so the same server can serve Copilot Studio and other A I clients.
In Copilot Studio its transport must be Streamable H T T P.
The older S S E transport is no longer supported.
Computer use operates websites and desktop apps with vision and reasoning, as if a person were looking at the screen.
Both need generative orchestration.
Computer use costs five Copilot Credits per step with standard models.
Your turn.
A maker connects an M C P server to an agent that still uses classic orchestration.
They want a topic to call its tools, but the tools never run.
What must change?
Call the M C P tools from inside a topic?
Switch the server transport to S S E?
Or switch to generative orchestration?
Decide before I answer.
Switch to generative orchestration.
M C P only works when the agent plans for itself.
Topics cannot call it, and S S E is no longer supported.
Keep two ideas apart.
Tools are for doing things.
Knowledge is for answering questions.
One knowledge type is unstructured data: files from OneDrive or SharePoint, synced and vector indexed in Dataverse, plus third party articles that arrive through connectors.
And when the agent picks a tool, it reads the tool's name and description.
A vague description makes it choose badly, or choose nothing.
Write it as if you were explaining the tool to a new teammate.
Your turn.
Contoso records invoices in an old desktop program.
It has no A P I and nobody can reach its database, but Nexo must type each new invoice into it.
Which bridge fits?
Computer use, working its screen?
A custom connector to the program?
Or an M C P server running on the program?
Decide before I answer.
Computer use.
There is only a screen, so Nexo works it with vision.
A connector and M C P both assume an A P I.

scenes.title: Add a tool in the studio

sentences.text: Here is how it looks in the studio.
Open Nexo and go to the Tools tab.
Select Add a tool and look at the categories: connectors, M C P, REST A P I, flows, and computer use.
Pick the bridge that fits the system.
For inventory, that is REST A P I with the OpenAPI file.
Write a clear name and description.
Create or select the connection, select Add to agent, and try it in the test pane.
Back to Valeria's three jobs.
The old invoice program gets computer use, which works its screen with vision.
Inventory, with its OpenAPI file, gets a REST A P I tool.
And because other A I clients in Contoso need the same tools, the team also exposes them as an M C P server.
Remember the question: does it have an A P I?
Then follow the order.
Next, who the agent is when it reaches those systems: identity and authentication.
